bullets.title: Semiconductor momentum unwind deepens; SOX down 28-29% from June peak
bullets.body: The SOX index has shed 28% over 26 trading days since its June 22nd peak, approaching the 32% decline seen in the first 24 days of the dot-com bust (March 2000). Long semis was BofA's most crowded trade in July and is now violently unwinding—Goldman traders report 'record selling' and 'violent derisking,' with GSPRHIMO (high-beta momentum pair) down 5.7% on day 3 of deleveraging, the largest 3-day de-gross on GS Prime since Nov '22. The 3x SOXL ETF is down 69% since June 22.

bullets.title: NVDA credit default swaps hit all-time high as bond market flashes warning
bullets.body: NVIDIA's CDS (credit default swaps) surged to an all-time peak, signaling record credit risk even as the stock retains some resilience. Bond market vigilantes are reasserting themselves with U.S. investment-grade yields near 22-year highs relative to S&P 500 earnings yields. A $240M NVDA dark pool print was also flagged intraday.

bullets.title: VRT drops 15% premarket on Q2 sales miss; AI data-center thesis intact per analysts
bullets.body: Vertiv fell 15% in premarket after Q2 net sales and organic growth missed consensus, with Morgan Stanley citing supply chain issues. However, the earnings call read-through is described as constructive for AI data-center infrastructure durability, with liquid cooling and water-efficient systems expanding TAM and Flex reporting senior-level hyperscaler discussions broadening the AI capex cycle beyond chips into power conversion and distribution.

bullets.title: MU trades at 5.4x forward P/E vs. 6.5x long-term avg; AI bottleneck stocks may be stabilizing
bullets.body: Micron is down 41% from its highs and now trades at 5.372x forward P/E versus its long-term average of 6.524x and a November peak of 12.6x. Analysts note the AI bottleneck basket's correlation with the rest of the S&P 500 fell to near-zero (0.01), suggesting independent price discovery. One analyst who has listened to ~20 earnings calls this season says the GAI infrastructure buildout thesis is unchanged and they are 'incrementally more bullish' despite stock underperformance.

bullets.title: SNDK plunges 56.6% from ATH to 15-month oversold extreme
bullets.body: Sandisk is down 56.6% from its June all-time high and hit a 15-month oversold level on technical indicators. Commentators noted a similar oversold reading in April 2025 preceded a historic rally, though some expressed disbelief that investors bought MU above $1,000 and SNDK above $2,000 earlier in the cycle.

bullets.title: Semiconductor equipment capex cycle structurally different: WFE could exceed $230B by 2028
bullets.body: A detailed thread argues the Street's $190–200B 2028 WFE consensus is too low: AMAT can double output with floor space ready, Lam nearly doubled capacity in four years, TEL targets 1.8x by FY2029, and ASML turned pre-emptive on capacity after 2Q26. ASML flagged like-for-like price increases; TSMC cited tool price inflation as the major driver of its +15% capex guide; Chinese customers reportedly agreeing to +10% DUV price increases. Suppliers (Ichor, Ultra Clean) still lack pricing power, with gross margins capped in an 8–21% band regardless of demand environment.

bullets.title: LITE: CHIPS Act silicon photonics play; management meeting notes published
bullets.body: The US government is taking a 1% stake in GFS and awarding $300M under the CHIPS Act specifically targeting co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon photonics—positioning Lumentum (LITE) as a beneficiary. Separately, AurelionRsch published management meeting notes from LITE's VP of IR plus third-party device engineer commentary. One analyst is skeptical on AAOI's $5.6B 2027 revenue target given the $6.3B current valuation, flagging indiscriminate AI deleveraging hitting high-beta names.

bullets.title: Fed uncertainty at historic extreme; Kalshi prices 77% hold / 23% hike
bullets.body: Bespoke describes pre-FOMC uncertainty as unprecedented; $69M was bet on Kalshi for this meeting vs. $3M for June. Fed futures markets price a one-third chance of a hike—Goldman Sachs notes whatever the decision will be 'the largest surprise at a non-rate-cut meeting since 1997.' JPMorgan base case is a hawkish hold (50% probability), projecting S&P 500 flat to -0.5%; a dovish hold (28%) could lift +1%. Former Fed adviser Jon Faust expects no hike, citing NY Fed President Williams's view that a 'credibility dividend' from surprise is not a factor. Warsh has abandoned forward guidance in favor of data-dependency since June.

bullets.title: META: strong Q2 expected; Zuckerberg calls for US AI acceleration; GEM model unlocks new compute demand
bullets.body: Multiple accounts expect a strong META quarter driven by LLM adoption and social's growing share of organic traffic from Google Search. Zuckerberg publicly called for the US to accelerate AI development. A separate thread highlights META's GEM foundation model showing LLM-style scaling laws now apply to recommendation systems, implying massive new compute demand far beyond current language-model spending.

bullets.title: MSFT earnings AH: Azure at record growth pace; Disney reportedly ditching GitHub Copilot for OpenAI Codex
bullets.body: Microsoft reports earnings after the bell with Azure described as growing at a record pace, though MSFT stock is down ~20% year-over-year. A negative pre-print signal: Disney is reportedly switching from Microsoft's GitHub Copilot to OpenAI's Codex, signaling potential enterprise AI customer churn ahead of results.

bullets.title: ARM touts 4x agentic AI efficiency; CRWV CDS at 850bps
bullets.body: ARM claims its architecture delivers 120M CPU cores per gigawatt for agentic AI workloads versus 30M previously—a 4x improvement—positioning it competitively in power-constrained deployments. Separately, CoreWeave (CRWV) is down 67% from ATH with CDS trading around 850bps; commentators used this as a benchmark for hypothetical OpenAI credit spread pricing.

bullets.title: TSLA breaks below $300, exits $1T market cap club; UBER continues to outperform
bullets.body: Tesla broke below $300, losing its trillion-dollar valuation. Multiple accounts note TSLA's consistent underperformance vs. UBER since 2024, with one long-term UBER holder arguing the company can compete with autonomous fleets via multi-partner sourcing. A valuation-focused account emphasizes that product quality and investment returns are distinct concepts for TSLA.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 enters technical correction; QQQ worst July since 1986
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 officially entered a technical correction (>10% from June ATH), with QQQ down ~9.5% in July—its worst month since September 2022 (prior bear market low) and worst July since July 1986. The S&P 500 Equal Weight (RSP) is simultaneously breaking to new all-time highs, a notable breadth divergence. Millions in QQQ puts accumulated ahead of FOMC; a $1.5B put wall sits at SPY 735.

bullets.title: Korean market contagion: leveraged ETF liquidation ~90% complete per JPMorgan
bullets.body: South Korean retail investors lost ~$25B in the past month from leveraged trading, with 62% of liquidated accounts belonging to investors aged 20–30. JPMorgan estimates hedge fund deleveraging is ~90% complete and most leveraged ETFs have been liquidated, but critics note JPM made a similar 'almost over' call 2,000 KOSPI points higher. KOSPI realized volatility is at levels seen only during major historical crashes. South Korea is capping retail exposure to leveraged ETFs and maintaining 24-hour market monitoring.

bullets.title: Crude oil surges 6–8% on Trump Iran threats; LNG tanker struck at Damietta port
bullets.body: WTI crude spiked 6–8% to above $86/barrel after Trump vowed to hit Iran 'hard' following US-Saudi strikes on Tehran-backed militias in Iraq. EIA data showed a 7.167M barrel crude draw vs. expectations of +256K, with Cushing inventories at tank bottoms. A US-owned LNG floating storage facility was struck by a drone at Egypt's Damietta port; no injuries or port facility damage reported and no group claimed responsibility.

bullets.title: Geopolitical macro: US sanctions Chinese entities over Iran ties; Hormuz open
bullets.body: The US Treasury sanctioned Chinese entities and oil tankers over Iran ties, specifically targeting 'Hormuz monetization.' CENTCOM states the Strait of Hormuz remains open for international traffic, with ~1,000 ships and 500M barrels assisted since May. European natural gas jumped 5.1% on Trump's Iran comments; Israel's defense establishment reportedly believes Washington is nearing a major counter-response to Iran.

bullets.title: BofA clients keep buying dip; Goldman warns of broader corr-1 macro event risk
bullets.body: BofA clients extended their equity buying streak to four consecutive weeks with institutional investors posting the largest weekly net purchases, even as the S&P dipped. However, Goldman's flows team warns 'risks of a correlation-1 macro event are creeping higher' and recommends buying protection. Goldman's High Beta Momentum basket is down 37% on the month.

bullets.title: STX reports third straight earnings triple play; TER revenue doubles YoY
bullets.body: Seagate Technology rallied over 5% on its third consecutive beat. Teradyne hit $1.33B in revenue, more than doubling year-over-year with Q3 guidance well ahead of consensus; one account flagged this as a positive read-through for COHU reporting tomorrow. Semiconductor equipment makers broadly (KLA, Teradyne, Advantest, ASM) beat Q2 estimates per the daily semi update.

bullets.title: DASH launches drone delivery division; AT&T Internet Air doubles subscribers
bullets.body: DoorDash confirmed it is building its own drone delivery aircraft via an internal robotics and autonomy team. AT&T's Internet Air fixed wireless product reached 2 million customers, doubling its subscriber base in approximately half the prior timeframe.

bullets.title: GLW worst single-day drop in 24 years on optical fiber capacity ceiling concerns
bullets.body: Corning posted its worst single-day decline in 24 years, driven by optical fiber capacity ceiling concerns. The drop was flagged as part of a broader day where SK Hynix fell 19% despite a six-fold profit surge, illustrating a market environment where strong fundamentals are being overwhelmed by positioning and macro factors.
